title: RBAC v2: policy compiler and transparent guardrail injector for API/runtime/console
creator: Marina Cortez
description: Problem: Current RBAC enforcement paths are duplicated across API gateway, runtime sidecars, and console UI which causes inconsistent deny/allow behavior, slow evaluation on high-QPS routes, and fragmented audit records. Goal: Ship a compiled RBAC v2 runtime artifact (policy compiler) that produces a compact evaluation DAG and a small runtime library, plus a transparent guardrail injector that can be deployed at API gateway, runtime, and console frontends to enforce the same compiled decisions. This ticket covers the compiler design, runtime library contract, guardrail injector proof-of-concept, console 'Simulate Role' admin control, and audit schema v2 integration.
acceptance_criteria: Policy compiler accepts high-level RBAC DSL and emits an optimized, deterministic bytecode/DAG that the runtime lib can evaluate with <=2ms median latency on amd64, <=10ms p99 at target QPS
Guardrail injector runs as a lightweight filter in API and runtime process and denies or annotates requests according to compiled artifact with no more than 1% added P99 latency to existing path
Console exposes a 'Simulate Role' control that lets admins run a request example through the same compiled policy and shows allow/deny decision + matched rule ID

Audit records emitted for each enforcement decision conform to audit schema v2 (fields: timestamp, request_id, principal, effective_roles, matched_rule, decision, reason, policy_snapshot_id) and appear in the centralized audit pipeline
SSO/SAML group-to-role mapping tests exercise mapping and fallback rules and are documented in the SSO mapping guide
Security review completed and formal approval from Security & Compliance on key material handling for policy artifacts and audit retention
notes: Design direction chosen to avoid runtime policy interpretation. Instead we compile to a small decision DAG with hash-indexed match nodes and an opt cache layer (HMAC-signed snapshots) to allow efficient verification across Dedicated and Private deployments. The guardrail injector will live behind a feature flag per-route and include a non-blocking fast path (cached allow) and a blocking slow path that consults compiled artifact. risks_mitigations: Risk: Policy artifacts could be tampered with during distribution to Private deployments. Mitigation: Sign artifacts with tenant-specific KMS keys and verify HMAC at ingestion time.
Risk: Compiled DAG growth for large enterprise rule sets may increase eval latency. Mitigation: implement rule partitioning and prefix-index slices; measurable limits in compiler with warnings.
Risk: Console simulate-role could leak sensitive request samples. Mitigation: require admin scope and redact payloads before evaluation when necessary; log simulate actions in audit stream.
Risk: Rollout causing unexpected denies. Mitigation: Canary the guardrail injector in 'observe' mode that annotates decisions without enforcing, and run comparison job for 48h before enforcement.
Risk: SSO group mapping ambiguity. Mitigation: explicit mapping precedence rules and an override table surfaced in console mapping UI.
